payload.title: How to Get Married in the Seychelles
payload.excerpt: The Seychelles is on your shortlist, and before you choose a bay or a resort you want to know one thing: will the marriage stand? In most cases, yes.
key_takeaways: Two Australians can marry legally in the Seychelles through a civil marriage registered by the Civil Status office, and in most cases Australia recognises it.
Every document you bring from home must be in English or French and carry an apostille.
The banns run for eleven days before the wedding, or a special marriage licence is normally issued within two days of applying.
Have your marriage certificate apostilled by the Supreme Court and authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs before you fly home.

faq.q: Is a Seychelles marriage recognised in Australia?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. An overseas marriage is generally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law. You cannot register it in Australia, and your Seychelles certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage.

faq.q: How early do we need to arrive in the Seychelles before the wedding?
faq.a: The banns run for eleven days before the wedding, and a special marriage licence, normally issued within two days, can shorten that wait. Arrange the registration with the Civil Status office before you fly, arrive at least two days before the ceremony, as the Australian High Commission advises, and leave time after it for the apostille.

faq.q: Can we marry on the beach in the Seychelles?
faq.a: Yes, with notice. The official wording calls this registering your marriage "at home", meaning somewhere other than the office, and asks for at least a week's notice to the office. The Australian High Commission says ceremonies may be held around the hotel with permission from the hotel and the Civil Registrar. Confirm the exact location with the office ahead.

faq.q: Do we need our own witnesses?
faq.a: Witnesses are a question for the Civil Status office. Ask whether they are needed, how many, whether you provide them yourselves and what identification they should bring, and settle it before you travel.

faq.q: Do our documents need an apostille?
faq.a: Yes. Every document issued overseas must be translated into English or French and apostilled. Your marriage certificate also needs an apostille from the Seychelles Supreme Court and a letter of authentication from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs before you leave.
